findings.title: withdraw() sends ETH before debiting credits, and the debit is unchecked
findings.description: withdraw calls msg.sender.call{value: amount}("") before decrementing credits[msg.sender], and the decrement is inside an `unchecked` block — a reentrant call from a malicious receive()/fallback can drain more than the caller ever deposited.

findings.title: unchecked block removes underflow protection on credits decrement
findings.description: Same root cause as f001 — checks-effects-interactions violation plus the unchecked subtraction that would otherwise revert on underflow. Duplicate report from a different angle (the subtraction site rather than the call site).

findings.title: setFeeRecipient has no access-control check
findings.description: Any caller, not just owner, can redirect protocol fees by calling setFeeRecipient directly. Contrast with pause() at line 21-22, which correctly checks msg.sender == owner.

findings.title: deposit() is vulnerable to reentrancy
findings.description: Claims deposit() makes an external call before updating state, enabling a reentrant drain. deposit() makes no external call at all — it only updates shares/totalShares. This claim does not match the code.

findings.title: Possible division by zero in withdraw() if totalShares is 0
findings.description: Claims amount = (shareAmount * balance) / totalShares can divide by zero. withdraw() requires shares[msg.sender] >= shareAmount first, and totalShares is only ever 0 before any shares exist — at which point no caller could hold a nonzero share balance to pass that check. Not reachable.
